p.seg: "Faulting the Qín - Part Two"
Qín extinguished the Zhou dynasty's sacrifices,
annexed the lands within the seas,
absorbed all the feudal lords,
faced south and claimed the title of Emperor,
and used the resources of the four seas to nourish the scholars of the world,
They eagerly turned towards him, admiring his influence.
Why was this so?
It is said:
For a long time, there had been no true king in recent antiquity.
The Zhōu dynasty was weak and declining.
After the Five Hegemons had passed,
its commands were no longer effective throughout the land.
Therefore, the feudal lords exerted their strength,
The strong oppress the weak,
the many tyrannize the few,
weapons of war do not cease,
the scholars and people are exhausted.
Now Qín faces south and reigns over all under Heaven,
it is as if there is a Son of Heaven above.
Therefore, the common people hope to secure their lives,
and all humbly look up to those above.
At this time,
to concentrate power and establish achievements,
the basis of security or danger lies in this.
The King of Qín harbors a greedy and base heart,
pursues self-striving wisdom,
does not trust meritorious officials,
is not close to the scholars and people,
abandons the way of kings and establishes private affection,
burns books and imposes cruel laws,
prioritizes deceitful force over benevolence and righteousness,
and takes tyranny as the beginning of its reign over the world.
were as before.
Chén Shè's position
was not more honorable than the lords of Qí, Chǔ, Yān, Zhào, Hán, Wèi, Sòng, Wèi, and Zhōngshān;
hoes and pitchforks
were not sharper than hooks, halberds, and long spears;
the conscripted masses
were not superior to the armies of the nine states;
profound strategy, long-term planning, and the art of deploying troops,
were not comparable to the scholars of those regions.
However, success and failure transformed,
accomplishments were opposite,
why is that?
If one were to let the states east of the mountains (Shāndōng) assess their relative size and measure against Chén Shè,
compare power and weigh strength,
then they could not be discussed in the same breath.
However, Qín, with its small territory,
attained the strength of ten thousand chariots,
brought the eight provinces into order and had equals come to court,
for more than one hundred years.
Afterwards, it took the entire world as its home,
and Hán'gǔ Pass as its palace.
(But) one man initiated a rebellion, and the ancestral temples fell,
the emperor died at the hand of another,
and was laughed at by the world,
why is that?
Benevolence and righteousness were not practiced,
and the positions of attack and defense were different.
trusted ministers and elite soldiers,
displayed sharp weapons, challenging those who passed.
Now that the realm was pacified,
in the heart of Shǐ Huáng,
he thought that the fortifications of Guānzhōng,
with its thousand *lǐ* of metal-walled cities,
would be a dynastic enterprise for his sons and grandsons for ten thousand generations.
After Shǐ Huáng died,
his remaining power still awed distant lands.
Yet Chén Shè, a son of a family with earthen jar windows and rope hinges,
a commoner,
and a conscripted migrant,
whose talent did not surpass that of the average person,
and who did not possess the wisdom of Zhòng Ní or Mò Dí,
or the wealth of Táo Zhū or Yī Dùn,
stepped out from the ranks of common soldiers,
and rose up from among the fields and paths,
leading weary and exhausted soldiers,
commanding a force of only a few hundred,
turned around and attacked Qín.
They chopped wood to make weapons,
and raised poles as banners,
and the world gathered like clouds in response,
bringing their own food and following like shadows,
and the heroes and elites of Shāndōng rose up together and destroyed the Qín clan.
Moreover, the empire was not small or weak;
the land of Yōngzhōu and the fortifications of Xiáo Hán
Jiǎ Yí's 新書, Volume 1
"Guò Qín Shàng"
Duke Xiào of Qín, relying on the strategic strength of the Xiáo and Hán Passes,
possessed the lands of Yōng Prefecture.
Sovereign and ministers guarded it firmly,
to spy on the house of Zhōu.
They had the intention to roll up the world like a mat,
to encompass the universe,
to bag the four seas,
and the ambition to swallow the eight wildernesses.
At this time,
Shāng Jūn assisted him,
establishing laws and standards internally,
focusing on agriculture and weaving,
and improving the implements for defense and warfare;
externally, he formed alliances and contended against the various lords.
Thereupon, the people of Qín folded their hands and seized the land outside the West River.
After Duke Xiào passed away,
Dukes Huìwén, Wǔ, Zhāo, and Xiāng inherited the old enterprise,
following the strategies left behind,
southward they took Hànzhōng,
westward they seized Bā and Shǔ,
eastward they cut off fertile land,
and northward they seized strategically important commanderies.
The feudal lords were fearful,
Huìméng ér móu ruò Qín.
They did not begrudge precious utensils, valuable treasures, or fertile lands,
in order to attract scholars from across the land.
They formed alliances and strengthened their relationships,
uniting with each other as one.
At that time,
Qi had Mèngcháng,
Zhao had Píngyuán,
Chu had Chūnshēn,
Wei had Xìnlíng:
these four lords,
were all wise and trustworthy,
generous and loving to the people,
respectful of the worthy and valued scholars.
They agreed on alliances and broke off treaties,
uniting the forces of Han, Wei, Yan, Zhao, Song, Wei, and Zhongshan.
Thereupon, among the scholars of the six states were Níng Yuè, Xú Shàng, Sū Qín, and Dù Hè and their like to advise them,
Qí Míng, Zhōu Zuì, Chén Zhěn, Shào Huá, Lóu Huǎn, Dí Jǐng, Sū Lì, and Yuè Yì and their followers to communicate their intentions,
and Wú Qǐ, Sūn Bìn, Dài Tuó, Ní Liáng, Wáng Liào, Tián Jì, Lián Pō, and Zhào Shē and their like to control their armies.
They once used land ten times the size,
and an army of a million,
to attack Qin from the passes.
The people of Qin opened the passes to welcome the enemy,
and the armies of the nine states hesitated, retreated, and dared not advance.
Qin did not waste a single arrow or arrowhead,
yet the feudal lords of the world were already in dire straits.
Thereupon, the alliances scattered and the agreements were broken,
competing to cede land to bribe Qin.
Qin had surplus strength to control their weaknesses,
pursuing the defeated and chasing those who fled north,
corpses piled up by the millions,
blood flowed enough to float shields,
taking advantage of the situation,
carving up the world,
Thereupon, he discarded the ways of the former kings,
burned the words of the hundred schools,
in order to make the common people ignorant.
He demolished famous cities,
killed heroes and outstanding men,
collected all the weapons of the realm and gathered them in Xiányáng,
melted down the sharp edges and arrowheads,
and cast them into twelve bronze statues,
in order to weaken the people of the realm.
Then he used the steep heights as city walls,
and used the river as a moat,
relying on heights of hundreds of millions of *zhàng*,
and overlooking unfathomable abysses as fortifications.
Good generals and strong crossbows guarded crucial and strategic places,
Now, those who conquer through unification value deceitful force,
those who ensure security value adapting to circumstances,
speaking in this way,
acquisition and defense are different arts.
Although Qín emerged from the Warring States period to reign over the world,
its way did not change,
its government did not reform,
and it maintained the means by which it had acquired its power.
Being isolated and possessing it,
therefore its downfall could be established and awaited.
Supposing the King of Qín (Qín Wáng) had discussed the affairs of past generations,
incorporating the precedents of Yīn and Zhōu,
in order to control his government,
even if later there were licentious and arrogant rulers,
there still would not have been the calamity of collapse.
Therefore, the three kings in establishing the world,
had glorious and beautiful names,
and their achievements were long-lasting.
Now that Qín Èrshì is established,
the world is not refraining from craning their necks and watching for its demise.
A cold person benefits from coarse clothes, and a hungry person is content with dregs and husks,
the world is clamorous,
this is the capital for a new ruler.
This is to say that oppressing the people is an easy way to practice benevolence.
Had Èrshì instead followed the conduct of a mediocre ruler,
and employed loyal and worthy men,
if the ruler and his ministers were of one mind and concerned about the troubles within the realm,
wearing mourning clothes and correcting the errors of the late emperor,
dividing land and people to enfeoff the descendants of meritorious officials,
establishing states and appointing rulers to treat the world with propriety,
emptying the prisons and abolishing punishments,
abolishing the sins of confiscating wives and children,
allowing each to return to their hometowns,
opening the granaries,
distributing wealth and currency,
To provide relief to the orphaned, solitary, poor, and distressed,
to lighten taxes and reduce impositions,
to assist the people in their emergencies,
to simplify laws and reduce punishments in order to maintain order thereafter,
to enable all people under Heaven to reform themselves,
to change their behavior and cultivate themselves,
to be cautious about their own conduct,
to fulfill the hopes of the myriad people,
and to bring peace to the world with supreme virtue.
Then within the four seas,
everyone would happily and peacefully enjoy their place,
fearing any change.
Even if there were cunning and harmful people,
they would have no thought of leaving their ruler.
Then rebellious ministers would have no way to disguise their wisdom,
and the evil of violence and disorder would be stopped.
Èr Shì did not practice this method,
but instead burdened the people with immorality,
destroying the ancestral temples,
and starting anew with the people.
He built the Āfáng Palace,
increased penalties and severe punishments,
and the officials' governance was harsh and exacting.
Rewards and punishments were inappropriate,
and taxes were levied without measure.
There were many troubles under Heaven,
and the officials could not record them all.
The people were impoverished, and the ruler did not provide relief.
然後 jiānwěi bìng qǐ,
those above and below evaded each other.
Those burdened with crimes were many,
executions and punishments were visible all along the roads,
and the world suffered because of it.
From the village communities down to the common people,
everyone harbored a heart of self-endangerment,
personally endured the reality of poverty and hardship,
all felt insecure in their positions,
therefore they were easily moved [to action].
This is why Chén Shè did not need the wisdom of Tāng and Wǔ,
nor did he borrow the honor of dukes and marquises.
He raised his arm in the marsh, and the world responded,
because his people were in danger.
Therefore, the former kings
saw the changes from beginning to end,
and knew the causes of survival and ruin.
Therefore, they governed them with the Way,
and strived only to bring them peace.
Even if there were ministers who acted rebelliously below,
they would certainly have no responding support.
Therefore it is said, "To pacify the people is to be able to practice righteousness,
but to endanger the people is easy to engage in wrongdoing,"
this is what is meant.
To be noble as the Son of Heaven,
to be wealthy with all within the Four Seas,
yet to find oneself subject to execution,
is the fault of the government.
This is the fault of Èr Shì.
The Qín dynasty annexed the feudal lords and the thirty-odd commanderies east of the mountains,
inspected the fords and passes,
occupied the dangerous passes and blockades,
repaired armor and weapons, and guarded them.
Yet Chén Shè (陳涉) led a disorganized crowd of several hundred men,
raised his arms and shouted loudly.
They didn't use bows and halberds,
but hoes and white staffs,
eating while looking towards houses,
and roamed freely throughout the land.
The people of Qín (秦) relied on the dangerous terrain but didn't defend it,
the passes and bridges were not closed,
long halberds did not stab,
and strong crossbows did not shoot.
Chǔ (楚) and Pèi (沛) penetrated deeply,
fought at Hóng Mén (鴻門),
and encountered no difficulty from even a fence.
Consequently, the area east of the mountains was greatly disturbed,
the feudal lords rose up together,
and heroes and talents established themselves.
Qín (秦) sent Zhāng Hán (章邯) to lead the eastern expedition.
Zhāng Hán (章邯), taking advantage of his large army, made deals in the marketplace outside [the capital],
to plot against his superiors.
That the officials did not trust each other
can be seen from this.
Zǐ Yīng (子嬰) ascended the throne but still didn't realize the situation.
Supposing Zǐyīng had the talent of a mediocre ruler,
and only obtained a middling assistant,
even though Shandong was in chaos,
the lands of the Three Qins could have been completely possessed,
and the ancestral temples should not have been cut off.
The Qin territory was secured by mountains and rivers,
a country with four strategic passes.
From Duke Mù onwards,
until the King of Qin,
more than twenty rulers,
were always the most powerful among the feudal lords.
Was this because they were all wise in every generation?
Their strategic advantage was obvious.
Moreover, the world had once united and joined forces to attack Qin.
During that time,
the wise and intelligent were aligned,
good generals deployed their armies,
wise ministers communicated their strategies,
but they were trapped by the perilous obstacles and could not advance.
Qin then lured them into battle and opened the passes for them,
leading to millions of soldiers fleeing north and ultimately collapsing, being trapped by the perilous obstacles and unable to advance.
Was it because they lacked courage, strength, or wisdom?
The circumstances were unfavorable,
and the situation was disadvantageous.
Although Qin was a small city,
it conquered and annexed large cities,
defending passes with their armies,
Build high ramparts and do not fight;
Close the passes and defend the strategic points;
Carry halberds and guard them.
The lords arose from commoners,
Meeting for profit;
They do not possess the virtuous conduct of a true king.
Their alliances are not yet strong,
Their people are not yet attached,
They claim to be destroying Qín,
But in reality, they are seeking personal gain.
When they see that Qín is difficult to conquer,
They will surely retreat.
Pacify the soldiers and give rest to the people,
Waiting for them to exhaust themselves.
Receive those who disband and execute the rebellious,
In order to command the feudal lords.
You need not worry about not getting your way in the realm.
Though honored as the Son of Heaven,
And possessing the wealth of the four seas,
If one is captured like a bird,
It is because the way to remedy the defeat was wrong.
The King of Qín was self-satisfied and did not ask for advice;
He continued in his mistakes without changing.
The Second Emperor received the throne,
And followed the same path without altering it,
Increasing the disaster with cruelty and tyranny.
Zǐyīng was isolated and without relatives,
Wēi ruò wú fǔ. Weak and without support.
Sān zhǔ zhī huò, Bewilderment of three rulers,
zhōngshēn bù wù, never comprehending throughout their lives,
wáng, they perished,
bù yì yí hū? is this not fitting?
Dāng cǐ shí yě, At this time,
shì fēi wú shēnmóu yuǎnlǜ zhī huà zhī shì yě, it was not that the world lacked scholars with deep plans, far-sighted considerations, and knowledge of change;
rán suǒyǐ bù gǎn jìnzhōng fúguò zhě, yet the reason they dared not fully offer loyalty and correct errors
Qín sú duō jìhuì zhī jìn yě, was that Qin customs had many prohibitions and taboos.
Zhōngyán wèi zú yú kǒu ér shēn mí méi yǐ. Before loyal words could finish leaving their mouths, their bodies were ground to pieces.
Gù shǐ tiānxià zhī shì, Therefore, the scholars of the world were made to
qīng ěr ér tīng, prick up their ears and listen,
zhòng zú ér lì, stand on tiptoe,
hé kǒu ér bù yán. close their mouths and not speak.
Shìyǐ sān zhǔ shīdào, Therefore, the three rulers lost the way,
ér zhōngchén bù jiàn, zhìshì bù móu yě, and loyal ministers did not remonstrate, and wise scholars did not strategize.
Tiānxià yǐ luàn, The world was already in chaos,
jiānchén bù shàng wén, but treacherous ministers did not report it to the superiors.
Qǐ bù bēi zāi! How sad is this!
Xiānwáng zhī yōngbì zhī shāng guó yě, The former kings knew that obstruction and concealment harmed the state,
gù zhì gōngqīng dàfū shì, so they established dukes, ministers, high officials, and scholars
yǐ shì fǎ shè xíng, to oversee the laws and establish punishments,
ér tiānxià zhì. and the world was governed.
Qí qiáng yě, When it was strong,
jìn bào zhū luàn ér tiānxià fú; it prohibited violence and executed disorder, and the world submitted.
Qí ruò yě, When it was weak,
wǔ bà zhēng ér zhūhóu cóng; the Five Hegemons campaigned, and the feudal lords followed.
Qí xuē yě, When it was weakened,
By guarding internally and attaching externally, the state survives.
Therefore, in the Qin's heyday,
its profuse laws and strict punishments shook the world;
but when it declined,
the people resented and longed for change, and the whole country rebelled.
Therefore, the Zhou kings succeeded in obtaining the Way in sequence,
and lasted for over a thousand years without interruption.
Qin lost both the fundamental and the superficial,
so it could not last long.
From this perspective,
the principles of safety and danger are vastly different.
A common saying goes:
"Not forgetting past events
is a teacher for future events."
Therefore, when a gentleman governs a state,
he looks to ancient times,
examines the present age,
considers human affairs,
observes the principles of prosperity and decline,
considers the appropriateness of power and influence,
abandons and embraces things in order,
adapts and changes according to the times,
and thus prolongs the days and secures the state.
"Head of the Lineage."
Now, a younger brother plots to become the Eastern Emperor,
the son of his elder brother turns west to attack,
and now Wu has again reported this.
The Son of Heaven is at the peak of his years,
his actions are not excessively flawed,
and his virtuous influence is increasing.
Yet things are still like this.
How much more so with the powerful lords,
whose authority is ten times greater than this?
Yet, why is there so little peace in the world?
The kings of large states were infants in swaddling clothes,
and the tutors and advisors appointed by the Hàn are now in control of affairs.
After several years,
the kings of the feudal lords will mostly be crowned,
their blood and energy will be at their peak,
and the tutors appointed by the Hàn will retire and be unwilling to stay.
The advisors appointed by the Hàn will claim illness and be granted dismissal.
They themselves will preferentially appoint their own personal followers to positions from assistant and commandant upwards.
If this is the case,
is there any difference from what happened in Huáinán and Jìběi?
At this time, if you then wish to achieve peace and order,
even Yáo and Shùn would not be able to do it.
Therefore, your servant says:
The time is passing,
if your Majesty does not plan for it early,
I fear that within a year, things will become what you do not desire.
The Yellow Emperor said:
"The sun at its zenith declines,
to wield a knife is surely to cut."
Now, to make this situation smooth and completely secure
It is very easy.
(But you) are unwilling to do it early.
Afterward, you cast aside those related to you by blood and kin, and resist those who would cut you down.
How is this different from the late years of the Qín 秦 dynasty?
Moreover, to say that Heaven has some power that is not very strange and frequently controls people,
How can this be obtained?
Now, with the position of the Son of Heaven,
Using the power of the Son of Heaven,
Taking advantage of the present time,
Relying on Heaven's assistance,
You still fear turning danger into safety,
Turning chaos into order.
Supposing Your Majesty were in the position of Qí Huán 齊桓 (Duke Huan of Qi),
Would you not unite the feudal lords and rectify the world?
To this extent, Your Majesty is greatly mistaken.
The time is about to be lost.
My heart secretly leaps, it is difficult to leave before this spring.
When Heaven is collapsing, time is collapsing, and strength is collapsing,
How can one be blind to this and unwilling to manage the loss of this collapsing time?
Would it not be ruinous?
One could benefit the world and be praised,
But especially because of these records.
I secretly feel very pained for Your Majesty.
I hope Your Majesty will retain (this) advice, even for a little while.
"Shù Níng 數寧" (Possibly a title, place name or person's name)
I humbly consider the situation,
One thing is regrettable,
There are two things for which one might shed tears,
and six things for which one might let out a long sigh.
As for other matters that are doubly unreasonable and harmful to the Way,
it is difficult to exhaustively enumerate them.
Those who offer counsel all say:
"The empire is already at peace."
I alone say:
"It is not at peace."
Some say:
"The empire is already well-governed."
I alone say:
"It is not well-governed."
I fear that going against your will will incur the death penalty,
but even so,
it is truly not at peace,
it is truly not well-governed,
therefore I dare not consider my own safety,
and dare to risk death to report it.
Those who say the empire is at peace and well-governed
are either extremely foolish and ignorant,
or deliberately flattering;
they are all people who do not know the true nature of order and chaos.
To hold fire and place it under a pile of firewood, and then sleep on top of it,
before the fire has caught,
and then call it safe,
is to steal temporary ease;
the current situation,
how is it different from this!
Now, when the fundamental and the superficial are inverted,
the beginning and the end are abruptly severed,
and the state's systems are chaotic,
it is clearly not a well-ordered state.
How can this be called governance!
Why doesn't Your Majesty issue an order to allow me a few days,
so that I can thoroughly understand the situation before you,
and then present plans for peaceful governance?
Your Majesty can then choose among them.
What great harm could there be?
Which is more urgent, the pleasure of hunting or the mechanisms of safety and danger?
Which is more pressing?
I have heard that
from Yǔ 禹 onward, after five hundred years, Tāng 湯 arose;
from Tāng 湯 onward, after five hundred years or more, King Wǔ 武王 arose.
Therefore, the rise of sage kings
is generally marked by five hundred years.
It has been more than five hundred years since King Wǔ 武王,
so why is it strange that a sage king has not arisen!
As for Qín Shǐ Huángdì 秦始皇帝,
he seemed to be one, but in the end, he was not,
and ended in disgrace.
Now that the world is gathered under Your Majesty,
I observe your broadness and understanding,
and I privately say:
because you are managing a chaotic inheritance,
and grasping a precarious situation,
If the worthy men of today,
are intelligent and capable enough,
and heavenly principles are also fitting,
it is appropriate for Heaven to ask Your Majesty to do it,
but if it is still not done,
then who else is one waiting for?
To make governing involve toiling with thought and consideration,
and afflicting the body,
lacking the pleasures of riding, drumming, and music,
should not be done.
The joy would be the same as now,
but with added constant peace,
and no worries in all directions,
because the various lords are attached and close, and follow the proper path,
offering loyalty and believing in the ruler.
Because the ruler does not doubt his ministers,
there are no clan punishments,
weapons of war are not mobilized,
and the people can long preserve their heads.
Because virtue extends to the most distant places,
the nearest being the Xiōngnú,
and the farthest being the four remote regions,
wherever human footprints can reach,
all admire the customs and yearn for righteousness,
and are happy to be subjects and sons.
Because the world is wealthy and sufficient,
resources are abundant,
and people have enough food for ten years.
Because the people are naturally simple,
they are compliant and happily follow orders.
Because official affairs are very simple,
lawsuits and bandits can be made few.
Once the great principle is grasped,
then the empire will be smoothly governed,
the atmosphere within the realm,
will be pure, harmonious, and completely ordered,
then all living things will flourish.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Only by governing in accordance with the spirits can one increase longevity."
Fà Zǐ said:
"In the ultimate of perfect governance,
fathers do not die before their sons,
elder brothers do not die before their younger brothers,
on the roads there are no burials of infants in swaddling clothes,
each dies with their natural lifespan."
The methods of grain and food
are indeed enough to satisfy everyone;
then the longevity of the most exalted will easily exceed a hundred years.
In ancient times, all Five Emperors lived beyond a hundred years.
Believing in this saying,
if the king is a wise emperor,
and his trusted officials are wise ministers,
the beauty of their reputation
will be passed down to infinity.
The *Rites* state that ancestors are honored for their merit, while founders are honored for their virtue.
Initially taking the empire is merit,
To govern the empire by virtue from the beginning,
and based on observing the temple of Chéng (successful precedent),
to establish the Emperor as Tàizōng (Grand Ancestor) for the empire,
inheriting the empire from Tàizǔ (Great Ancestor),
would mean the Hàn dynasty would last without end.
Because the humble do not doubt the honored,
and the lowly do not overstep the noble,
with honor, humility, nobility, and lowliness,
as clear as black and white,
then the masses of the empire would have no doubts or confusion.
Because managing affairs is based on heaven and earth,
and laws and policies rely on the four seasons,
future generations would have no unexpected events,
and no changes to the norm,
simply following the path and lasting for a long time.
Your subject secretly believes that establishing a state of lasting peace,
achieving a lasting governance,
in order to serve the ancestral temple,
and to provide for the six kinds of relatives,
is the utmost filial piety;
to govern the empire,
and to manage all living beings,
so that spirits and people are all satisfied,
and the altars of the land and grain are enjoyed for a long time,
is the utmost benevolence;
to establish classics and set forth regulations,
balancing what is light and heavy, comprehensive and appropriate,
so that later generations can use them as a model of law for ten thousand generations,
Afterwards, even if there are foolish, young, and unworthy successors,
they would still be able to inherit the legacy and live in peace,
which is perfectly clear.
(This would result in) a lifespan comparable to the Five Emperors,
and the benefits extending far and wide.
What loss would there be to Your Majesty?
With Your Majesty's wisdom and understanding,
if you would only allow those who have some knowledge of governance to assist you,
achieving this state of order would not be difficult.
Why doesn't Your Majesty give it a try?
While the details can be presented to you in advance,
I hope that you will not disregard them.
Your servant has carefully examined the principles of heaven and earth,
verified them against ancient history,
and considered the affairs of the present time.
Day and night, I have pondered this to the point of familiarity.
I can only sigh with sorrow and indignation,
and dare not neglect it at any time.
Even if Yǔ 禹 and Shùn 舜 were to be reborn,
and make plans for Your Majesty,
how could they change this?
There is a method to achieve this,
which will surely ensure complete safety without harm.
Your servant dares to stake his life on it.
Your Majesty, please summon knowledgeable ministers and have them evaluate it.
If there is anyone who believes it is disadvantageous to the emperor and harmful to the world,
I will gladly die.
"Fān Shāng" (On Injuring a Vassal)
Generally, in establishing a state, one must carefully examine the forces of mutual suspicion.
If those below are frequently afflicted by misfortune,
and those above are frequently burdened with worry,
and disastrous famines frequently occur,
then surely there will be monstrous things born from it.
The calamities that befall,
how can they be foreseen?
Therefore, excess is not the way to secure the ruler above,
nor is it the way to protect great ministers,
nor is it the way to keep beloved sons safe.
Once you have already appointed someone to be a vassal,
to be a subject of another,
and then increase his power,
enhance his authority,
causing him to have an arrogant heart and be difficult to obey,
how is that different from skillfully sharpening a Móyé sword and handing it to Yè Shè (射子),
certain self-inflicted disaster?
To truly love them is certainly to allow them to indulge in the taste of rich food,
enjoy the sound of metal and stone instruments,
have a multitude of subjects and people,
broad territories,
sufficient to provide for and protect their persons.
However, their power should not be enough to seek undue favor,
their influence should not be enough to commit rebellion.
Thus, they will have no arrogant heart,
no wicked deeds,
they will uphold the law and fear commands,
Listening and obeying is surely smooth sailing,
long life and peace,
and there will be no calamity of suspicion between superiors and inferiors;
preserving high ministers,
and protecting beloved sons,
who is more adept at this?
Moreover, regarding the system of feudal states,
the power is not merely small,
the system dictates: those who have sons, let the country be given to their sons,
those who do not yet have sons, establish a branch to await them,
when a son is born, he is established,
their body and their sons,
what loss would there be?
In reality, there is no loss, and the country is preserved without worry,
descendants generation after generation will need the Hàn,
all like Chángshā,
this can last long indeed,
it is the so-called bringing life back to the dead and flesh to bare bones,
why enrich them?
"Fortifying the Borders"
furtively examines past events,
generally, the powerful ones revolt first.
The Huáiyīn King of Chǔ was the most powerful,
therefore he rebelled first;
Hán Wáng Xìn relied on the Hú,
therefore he rebelled again;
Guàn Gāo relied on the resources of Zhào,
Then he would rebel again;
Chén Xī’s troops were elite and strong,
then he rebelled again;
Péng Yuè controlled Liáng,
then he rebelled again;
Qíng Bù controlled Huáinán,
then he rebelled again;
Lú Wǎn's state in the north was the weakest,
so he rebelled last.
Chángshā only had twenty-five thousand households,
their strength was insufficient to carry out rebellion,
so their achievements were few but they were most complete,
their position was weak, so they were most loyal,
when all families were being exterminated,
Chángshā had no incident,
it was not solely because their nature differed from others,
but because of their situation.
In the past, if Fán, Lì, Jiàng, and Guàn had controlled dozens of cities and been made kings,
even if they were ruined and perished now, it would have been acceptable;
if Hán Xìn, Qíng Bù, and Péng Yuè and their like had been made marquises with stipends and lived peacefully,
even if they existed until now, it would have been acceptable.
Therefore, the great plan for the empire is knowable.
If you want all the kings to be loyal and attached,
it would be best to make them like the King of Chángshā;
if you want the ministers not to be minced and pickled,
it would be best to make them like Fán, Lì, Jiàng, and Guàn;
if you want peace and order in the empire and the emperor to have no worries,
it would be best to establish many feudal lords but reduce their power.
If one's strength is small, they are easily governed by righteousness;
if a state is small, it has no wicked intentions.
If one engages in mutual slaughter with their subjects,
and consumes their own flesh and blood,
even if the world is in danger, there will be no harm,
then it is best to follow the old ways and not change.
Looking at the past,
those states that were the largest,
were the first to fall.
"The Great Cities"
Formerly, King Líng of Chǔ asked Fàn Wúyǔ,
"I wish to greatly build up the cities of Chén, Cài, Yè, and Bùgēng,
and equip each with a thousand chariots.
Would that be enough to rival Jìn?
If I add to that the strength of Chǔ,
would the feudal lords come to pay tribute?"
Fàn Wúyǔ said,
"It is not possible.
I have heard that great cities arouse suspicion of the state,
and powerful ministers arouse suspicion of the ruler;
they are the means of chaos.
If cities are suspected, then there will be mutual contention;
if ministers are suspected, then they will issue conflicting orders;
these are the deepest sources of disaster.
Now, if you greatly build up the cities of Chén, Cài, Yè, and Bùgēng,
and perhaps they are not sufficient,
they will not be enough to intimidate Jìn;
If you were to fill them with resources,
and staff them with ministers of great emolument,
this would be to slight the root and emphasize the branch.
I have heard that a tail too big cannot be wagged,
and a branch too big will surely break.
Is this not using your authority to impress the feudal lords?
However, the great affliction for the state of Chǔ will ultimately
certainly be these four cities."
King Líng Wáng did not listen,
and indeed fortified Chén, Cài, Yè, and Bùgēng,
staffing them with war chariots,
and filling them with high ministers.
In that year,
the feudal lords indeed paid court.
After several years,
Chén, Cài, Yè, and Bùgēng,
some supported the young master Qìjí internally to create trouble.
The state of Chǔ was thrown into chaos.
The King then died in the well of Yù Yǐn Shǒu Hài in Gān Xī.
To have planned in this way,
how could it not be painful?
Alas!
The root is small and the branch is large,
laxity will surely lead to disloyalty.
Time! Time!
This is what is regrettable.
The state of the world
is suffering from a great tumor.
A leg is as large as the waist,
a finger is as large as the thigh.
I have heard that a tail that is too large cannot be wagged,
and branches that are too large will be broken off.
This is a terrible disease.
In ordinary times, one cannot bend and stretch,
and if one or two fingers twitch,
the body will certainly be distressed.
If you fail to treat it now,
it will certainly become a chronic illness,
and even if you have Biǎn Què later,
he will not be able to do anything about it.
Alas!
If the branches grow too large,
the laxity will certainly reach the heart.
This is why I secretly worry about Your Majesty.
The illness is not merely swollen feet,
but also suffers from dissension.
The son of Yuán Wáng
is the emperor's cousin;
the current kings
are the sons of cousins.
The sons of Huì Wáng
are the sons of close elder brothers;
the current kings
are the grandsons of brothers.
Those who are close may not be granted land to secure the empire,
while those who are distant may monopolize great power to coerce the Son of Heaven.
Your servant has previously stated that it is not merely a matter of suffering from swollen feet [zhǒng yě],
but also from the pain of twisted and contrary principles [cuī lì yě].
What is truly lamentable
is this affliction.
In the *Děng Qí* ("Equal Standards") regulation,
the guards in the palaces where the feudal lords and kings reside,
and the crafting of shoes by humble artisans [zhī lǚ dūn yí],
when assessed according to the imperial standards applicable to the emperor's palaces,
with the gentlemen-in-waiting and announcers receiving audiences and conveying messages,
doing so according to the regulations governing audiences with the emperor;
if in serving the feudal lords and kings, there is a lack of integrity or fairness,
they are punished according to the laws applicable to serving the emperor.
Saying "everything is done according to the laws of Hàn,"
serving the feudal lords and kings is essentially serving the emperor.
This implies that the feudal lords and kings are equal to the supreme sovereign.
If that is the case, then the relationship between the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords,
and between a subject and his inferiors,
should they really be so meticulously and equally the same [zhuàn rán qí děng ruò shì hū]?
The advisor to the Son of Heaven
is titled Chancellor [chéngxiàng]
and given a golden seal;
the advisor to the feudal lords
is titled Chancellor [chéngxiàng]
and given a golden seal.
Yet, there is no distinction in their honor.
Their salary is above 2,000 piculs of grain.
The Son of Heaven's high officials receive a salary of 2,000 piculs of grain,
The feudal lords and ministers are of the rank of two thousand *shí*,
then your servant is already the same as them.
The ruler elevates his ministers and honors them,
but now your servant is already the same,
then how can the laws not be equal?
The emperor's personal guard
is called the Grand Coachman (*Dà Pú*),
[bears] a silver seal and a rank of two thousand *shí*;
the feudal lord's coachman
is called the Grand Coachman (*Dà Pú*),
[bears] a silver seal and a rank of two thousand *shí*;
then the coachmen are already the same,
if the coachmen are already the same,
then how can the decorations on the carriages not be the same?
The emperor's mother
is called Empress Dowager (*Tài Hòu*);
the feudal lord's mother
is called Empress Dowager (*Tài Hòu*);
the emperor's consort
is called Empress (*Hòu*);
the feudal lord's consort
is called Empress (*Hòu*).
Then what does the feudal lord lose, and what does the emperor gain?
If the wives are already the same,
then how are the husbands different?
The gate of the emperor's palace is called *Sīmǎ*;
one who enters without permission becomes a city wall builder;
the gate of the feudal lord's palace is called *Sīmǎ*;
one who enters without permission becomes a city wall builder;
the hall doors are both hall doors,
and the crime of entering without permission is also public execution.
The palace wall gate guards have the same name,
their severity is the same,
and the crimes are already equal.
